summary.short: Proposed Norwegian bill (Prop. 41 LS) amending the Copyright Act to implement EU Directives 2019/789 and 2019/790: country-of-origin rule for online broadcast services, press publishers' right, education and cultural heritage exceptions, text and data mining exceptions, platform liability, and remuneration and reporting duties. Commencement date not stated.
summary.long: Proposal (Prop. 41 LS, 2025–2026) to amend Norway's Copyright Act and related acts, implementing EU Directives 2019/789 (online broadcasting and retransmission) and 2019/790 (digital single market), and seeking consent to EEA Joint Committee Decisions 332/2023 and 333/2023 and to accession to the WIPO WCT and WPPT. Operative provisions add a press publication right for information society service providers with a two-year term (new §24a); amend education exceptions and licensing (§§43, 46, 47, 57); add out-of-commerce cultural heritage uses (§§49a, 50a–50c); create text and data mining exceptions for lawfully accessed works (§50e, with a rightholder reservation) and for research and cultural heritage institutions (§50f, with secure storage); add an annual reporting duty from acquirers of rights to authors (§69a) and a right to reasonable remuneration on transfer (§69); allow authors to revoke exclusive rights for non-use (§74); set liability and safe-harbour conditions for content-sharing service providers (§§86–86c); extend Copyright Board mediation and dispute powers (§§31a, 65–65f); and provide criminal fines or imprisonment up to one year for infringement (§79) and up to three years for gross infringement (§80). The fetched text does not state an entry-into-force date.

notes: Excerpt covers pp. 283-294 of Prop. 41 LS: the cover letter, the Stortinget request, the bill text amending åndsverkloven through § 86 c (cut off mid-sentence), and preparatory remarks for sections 23.2 to 23.4. Operative wording for the amendments to tvisteloven, the collective management act and the sports personal data act, and for new sections 115 a to 115 c, is not in the excerpt. Part B (EEA consent resolution) and the WIPO treaty accession consent are not annotated. Target IDs are not assigned in the registry, so target_instrument_id is left empty. Preparatory remarks note the amendments to the sports personal data act 'har ikke materiell betydning' (no material change), so they only restate existing law.
